shared-needs.rule: Each need names the shared volume and anchor that holds the rule; check.sh resolves it. A number written in a shared contract is cited, never restated here.
shared-needs.need: Rows for store.opened 100; record.committed 200 (replayed) and 201; record.invalid 400; record.refused 403; record.conflict 409 (version, id, idempotency_mismatch); record.stale 412 (stale_token, lease_not_current); store.restored 200; store.corrupt 500; store.wal_large 500; store.busy 503; store.disk 503; store.unavailable 503; stream.slow 503. Owner-acts: store.corrupt, store.unavailable, store.restored, store.disk after N-45 ran.
records(seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, epoch, id UNIQUE, at, code, kind, node, by, ticket, attempt, body JSON, hash); append-only; seq strictly increasing and never reused, not gapless.
entities(key PRIMARY KEY, kind, version, body JSON, updated_seq, updated_at); version grows by one per write.
idempotency(operation_key PRIMARY KEY, kind, node, request_hash, reply JSON, epoch, seq, at).
The forward-only migration table; the node owning a table owns its migration and registers its statements.
The record envelope; canonical JSON by RFC 8785 for the hash and the request hash.
Compare-and-swap on entity version; expected 0 inserts.
One store, no broker, SQLite under the state root, never in the repository.
Atomic writes, append-only records, fencing, compare-and-swap, idempotent steps, conflicts that report.
Retry up to 3, then recover and report.
quick_check not ok at open: NOT_SERVING, a prepared dry-run restore, never an automatic restore over the live file.
Free space under store.min_free_mib: commits refused 503 store.disk, N-45 cleanup first.

purpose.is: N-01 is the one durable store of the factory: every record, entity and node-owned table lives in one SQLite file on the WSL host, owned by the service user coq-svc and reachable only through one authenticated gRPC socket or in-process by the service's own nodes.
It is the carrier of every edge in the DAG: an output of any node is a Commit here, and the (epoch, seq) it returns is the cursor the push transport (N-31) fans out.

It is the authority check of every write: the caller's Unix identity, not a field it sends, decides which node it is and which kinds and statements it may write (shared/authority.xml#role-derivation).
purpose.is-not: It is not a broker, a bus or a queue daemon (D10, C34); no records branch, no records tree in the repository (D04, C35).
It decides nothing about work: routing, retry policy and verdicts live in N-07, N-11 and the gate nodes; a statement's guard is its owner's rule, registered by its owner.
purpose.decisions: D01 (Go service with gRPC owns state), D10 (one store, SQLite on the host, backups scheduled), D04 (artifacts in the state root), D22 (the service on the WSL host); review dispositions F01, F02, F04, F07, F14, F15 (shared/review-dispositions.xml).

record.who: Every node of the service in-process (Store.Do), the owner's ctl CLI and the launcher over the socket. Seats and pods have no socket and never call the store (shared/authority.xml#seat-isolation).
record.field: node/operation/subject/r<revision> per shared/contracts.xml#operation-keys; one key per intended effect; the node segment must equal the authenticated caller's node.
The lease reference {key, token} the writer acts under; fenced per shared/contracts.xml#fencing.
Entity versions that must hold at commit (0 means absent).
Entity compare-and-swap writes; null value deletes.
Owner-registered statements on node-owned tables (shared/contracts.xml#statements); no free SQL crosses the socket or the Tx.
0 to 16 records; each validates against its kind's schema; node and by are set by the server, never trusted from the caller.
Outbox intents written with the deciding record (shared/contracts.xml#outbox).

input.rule: A Commit is one transaction: every write it names commits together or none does. The old Put is a Commit with one record (record.schema.json#/$defs/record_put).
Limits come from shared/contracts.xml#batch (entity writes, statement rows, records, the transaction budget, no I/O inside); over a limit is 400 reason limits before BEGIN.

record.field: 201 committed; 200 replayed (same operation key, same request hash); 403, 409, 412, 423, 429, 503 refusals; 400 invalid is answered as record.invalid.
The store epoch and the seq of every record appended, in request order.
The entity versions after the write.

Assigned at commit by AUTOINCREMENT: strictly increasing and unique inside the store, never reused even after a delete, and not gapless (a rolled-back transaction or N-45 retention leaves gaps). A seq means something only with its epoch.
The store epoch (entity store:epoch, shared/contracts.xml#epoch-cursor); a restore starts a new one.
sha256 of the canonical JSON record.
true with code 200 when the operation key and request hash were already committed.
unknown_principal, kind_not_permitted, principal_mismatch, capability_expired (shared/authority.xml#role-derivation).
The peer uid and the principal it mapped to (none when unknown).
What was attempted; no other part of the request is stored.
version (an entity or precondition miss, with expected and current), id (a duplicate record id) or idempotency_mismatch (the operation key was committed with a different request hash).
stale_token (the token is not the lease's) or lease_not_current (the lease is released, expired or revoked, or its key is unknown).
Evidence; nothing else is written.

output.rule: Every refusal (400, 403, 409, 412) is appended as its own record in a separate transaction, so a refusal is visible, never silent; a storm of the same refusal from one principal is latched to one record per principal, reason and minute.

Entity-only kinds (ticks, health, heartbeats, page.state, watcher.alive; shared/contracts.xml#entity-only) are registered entity-only: their Commit writes the entity and appends no record unless the entity's state field changes.

api.rule: The real proto today is scheduler/api/scheduler/v1/scheduler.proto: Executor{Run, Health} and Scheduler{Health, Status, Reload, Drain, Retry}; nothing streams. This book adds three services; none of them exists yet, each is a planned file.

service.name: coq.store.v1.Store
service.rpc: An entity by key or a record by id; a read on a pooled reader connection.
Records after a cursor {epoch, seq}, filtered by kind, ticket or node, at most 1000 per page; next cursor returned.

Server stream of frames {epoch, seq, kind, id} after a cursor (shared/contracts.schema.json#/$defs/cursor). It replaces the "Subscribe" stream older volumes name. A cursor from another epoch, below min_retained_seq or above the high-water seq is refused OUT_OF_RANGE reason cursor.expired; the client takes a snapshot and resumes. A client not reading within 1 s is closed UNAVAILABLE reason stream.slow; the only Tail clients are N-31 and the ctl CLI, and the browser drop rule belongs to N-31.

VACUUM INTO a destination under STATE/backup/store/tmp/ on a dedicated reader connection; replies {epoch, high_water_seq, row_count, min_retained_seq, bytes} read from the copy, so the numbers describe exactly the image (N-05 verifies them).
grpc.health.v1; SERVING only when the file is open, quick_check passed and free space is above the floor.

api.service: Start, Renew, Release for the launcher (nodes/N-02/spec.xml#api).
Answer for the owner page and CLI.

map.note: a hold or a held lease guard

status-map.rule: Every error is a google.rpc.Status carrying google.rpc.ErrorInfo{reason, domain "coq.store.v1", metadata {code, operation_key}}; callers branch on the code and reason, never on message text.

api.deadlines: Commit: client deadline 5 s (enqueue plus transaction); the transaction itself is bounded by shared/contracts.xml#batch. Get and List 2 s. Snapshot backup.snapshot_seconds (N-05). Tail has no deadline; it is closed by stream.slow or the client.
api.compatibility: Fields are only added; a field number is never reused; `buf breaking` against main runs in the gate (planned check, scheduler/api/buf.yaml planned).

mechanism.component: One SQLite database: STATE/store/coq.db with its -wal and -shm. PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=FULL, busy_timeout=5000, foreign_keys=ON, wal_autocheckpoint=1000. STATE belongs to coq-svc, mode 0700 (shared/authority.xml#principals).

Go package scheduler/internal/store: Open, Do, Commit, Get, List, Tail, Snapshot, Close. In-process callers use Store.Do(ctx, op, fn(*Tx)) with the same steps as Commit; Tx offers Get, CAS, Delete, Next(counter), Append, Exec(registered statement), Fence(lease key, token), Effect(intent), and no other way to touch the file. The clock is core.Clock.
gRPC on /run/coq/store.sock, owner coq-svc, group coq-store, mode 0660, no TCP (shared/authority.xml#peer-credentials). The group holds the owner and coq-launch; seats get no socket.
One writer goroutine owns every write transaction; callers queue on a bounded channel (store.put_queue 256). Readers use a pool of read connections; Snapshot uses its own reader connection.
mechanism.tables: This node owns records, entities and idempotency (needs above), reads the principals table (shared/authority.xml#principals) and hosts the effects table (shared/contracts.xml#outbox). Other nodes own their tables and register their statements: leases (N-02), tickets and claims (N-03), forge (N-04), backups (N-05). records(seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, epoch, id UNIQUE, at, code, kind, node, by, ticket, attempt, body JSON, hash); append-only. entities(key PRIMARY KEY, kind, version, body JSON, updated_seq, updated_at); compare-and-swap on version. idempotency(operation_key PRIMARY KEY, kind, node, request_hash, reply JSON, epoch, seq, at).
mechanism.mermaid: sequenceDiagram participant C as caller (node in-process, ctl, launcher) participant S as Store gRPC participant W as writer goroutine participant DB as coq.db (WAL) C->>S: Commit(operation_key, lease?, preconditions, entities, statements, records, effects) S->>S: 0 authenticate SO_PEERCRED uid, derive node, by, kinds (403) S->>S: 1 validate shapes, kinds, limits (400) S->>W: enqueue (bounded, 5 s) W->>DB: BEGIN IMMEDIATE W->>DB: 2 idempotency by operation_key alt same request hash W-->>C: 200 replayed, stored reply else different hash W-->>C: 409 idempotency_mismatch else new W->>DB: 3 fence lease key and token (412) W->>DB: 4 preconditions, 5 entity CAS (409) W->>DB: 6 registered statements (owner guards) W->>DB: 7 append records (seq AUTOINCREMENT, epoch, node, by) W->>DB: 8 effects, 9 idempotency row W->>DB: COMMIT W-->>C: 201 epoch, seqs, versions W->>S: 10 notify Tail end
mechanism.step: Authenticate (shared/authority.xml#peer-credentials, #role-derivation): read SO_PEERCRED on the connection; map the uid through the principals table; unknown uid is 403 unknown_principal. The server derives node, by and the permitted kinds and statements of that principal; a record whose node or by disagrees, or an operation key whose node segment is not the derived node, is 403 principal_mismatch; a kind or statement outside the set is 403 kind_not_permitted; a launcher capability past its expiry is 403 capability_expired. In-process, the principal is coq-svc and the node is the one the op names; the same set check applies, so a node cannot write another node's kinds.

Validate: commit_request shape, each record against its kind's schema, codes in the live code table, the limits of shared/contracts.xml#batch; any failure is 400 record.invalid with the JSON pointer, before BEGIN.

Idempotency (shared/contracts.xml#operation-keys): request_hash is sha256 of the RFC 8785 canonical request with id, at, seq and hash removed from every record. A committed key with the same hash returns the stored reply with code 200 and replayed true; with a different hash it is 409 record.conflict reason idempotency_mismatch, before any effect.

Fence (shared/contracts.xml#fencing): when lease is present, the leases row for that key must be reserved or running, hold that token, and not be expired at commit; else 412 record.stale (stale_token or lease_not_current). The terminal-report exception of shared/contracts.xml#terminal-report is the only write accepted under a non-current token.
Preconditions: every named entity is at its expected version (0 = absent); else 409 reason version with expected and current.
Entity writes: compare-and-swap on version; a miss is 409 reason version; null deletes.

Statements: each is a prepared statement its owning node registered for its own table (shared/contracts.xml#statements); its guard, when it fails, answers the code its owner registered (for example N-02's lease guards 412, 423 or 429, N-03's claim overlap 412 precondition). A statement may append its owner's record in the same transaction.

Records: append each; seq from AUTOINCREMENT, epoch from store:epoch, node and by from step 0, hash over canonical JSON. An entity-only kind appends nothing unless its state changed (shared/contracts.xml#entity-only).
Effects: insert each intent as an effects row in state intent (shared/contracts.xml#outbox).

Write the idempotency row (operation_key, kind, node, request_hash, reply, epoch, seq), then COMMIT with synchronous FULL. A transaction over the budget of shared/contracts.xml#batch is rolled back and answered 503 store.busy reason limits.
mechanism.canonical: Canonical JSON: RFC 8785, UTF-8; the same function serves the record hash, the request hash and the backup checksum.
mechanism.ids: Record id as today: UTC stamp, code, five-character suffix; unique per writer; a duplicate is 409 reason id.
mechanism.epoch: Entity store:epoch {epoch, started_at, cause, min_retained_seq} (shared/contracts.schema.json#/$defs/store_epoch). Epoch 1 is written at creation; N-45 retention advances min_retained_seq in the same transaction that deletes rows; a restore starts the next epoch (#runbook). Every record, Tail frame and cursor carries the epoch.
mechanism.snapshot: Snapshot never takes the writer: VACUUM INTO runs on a dedicated reader connection as one read transaction, so the copy is one consistent image while commits continue; epoch, high_water_seq (max seq), row_count (count of records) and min_retained_seq are then read from the copy. Probe evidence at baseline (report D, a model of the store, not the built service): 293.7 MiB copied in 2.84 s with 9,788 writes committed and a maximum write latency of 184 ms. The built-service proof is not-run.

start.rule: Nothing starts by an agent typing. The system unit coq-svc.service (N-06) starts the binary as coq-svc; the store opens before any tick, and READY=1 is not sent until Health answers SERVING or the open has failed three times (then READY with NOT_SERVING, see retries).
start.step: Resolve the state root with bin/state-root.sh as coq-svc; a relative root is exit 3 and the unit fails loudly.
Create STATE/store/ 0700 when absent; open coq.db; apply migrations forward only; write store:epoch epoch 1 cause created when absent.
PRAGMA quick_check with a 60 s bound; ok starts serving; anything else is the corrupt path under retries.
SQLite replays the WAL on open. Append store.opened 100 with epoch, high-water seq and file size.
systemd creates /run/coq (RuntimeDirectory of coq-svc.service); listen on store.sock 0660 group coq-store; answer Health SERVING; N-06 starts the ticks.

wait.name: busy
wait.fallback: 503 store.busy to the caller; the caller retries per retries; no row is written

wait.name: put-queue
wait.fallback: 503 store.busy; counter store.queue_full increments; health degrades at 3 in one minute

wait.name: transaction
wait.fallback: rollback; 503 store.busy reason limits; the caller's op is retried by its owner, never split by the store

wait.name: quick-check
wait.fallback: treated as a failed open; recovery path

wait.name: checkpoint
wait.timeout: every 1000 pages or 60 s, whichever first; PASSIVE, TRUNCATE at drain
wait.fallback: a checkpoint that cannot complete 3 times in a row records store.wal_large 500 at 256 MiB

wait.name: tail-send
wait.fallback: the stream is closed UNAVAILABLE stream.slow; the client reconnects from its cursor, or snapshots on cursor.expired

wait.name: snapshot
wait.on: VACUUM INTO on the reader connection
wait.fallback: the reader connection is cancelled and the temp removed; N-05 counts a failed attempt; the writer was never held

wait.name: disk
wait.fallback: below store.min_free_mib the store deletes STATE/run/store.reserve once (shared/outside-probe.xml#journal) so the reporting commits have room, then refuses other commits with 503 store.disk and health goes unhealthy

wait.name: drain
wait.fallback: the process exits anyway; SQLite rolls back the open transaction on next open

retries.rule: Who retries a refusal is decided once, in shared/contracts.xml#retry-owner; the store never retries a caller's Commit and never splits one.
retries.step: A 503 is retried by the caller with the same operation key and the same request, so a retry is a replay or a first commit, never a double write; the count and backoff are the caller's layer in shared/retry-budget.xml#layers.

Open failing (lock, io, schema) is retried 3 times 5 s apart; then the unit stays up, Health answers NOT_SERVING and the /livez answer names reason store (shared/outside-probe.xml#probe). A store that cannot open cannot carry a card: the owner is told by the outside probe's alert (shared/outside-probe.xml#alerting), and store.unavailable is written to the outage journal STATE/run/emergency.jsonl, imported as a record on recovery (shared/outside-probe.xml#journal). The unit does not crash-loop on a bad file.

quick_check not ok: 3 attempts of integrity_check; still not ok means a dry-run restore listing from the newest verified backup is prepared at STATE/run/restore-plan.txt, store.corrupt 500 goes to the outage journal and the /livez reason, and the outside probe alerts. The store never restores over the live file on its own.
A 409 is never retried by the store; the caller re-reads and re-decides, at most 3 times, then writes its own failure record.

many-agents.reading: Every node and the ctl CLI read at once: WAL snapshot reads on a pool of connections, never blocked by the writer; List and Tail are keyed by (epoch, seq).
many-agents.working: No agent touches coq.db or the socket. Seats have neither; the launcher writes for them (shared/authority.xml#seat-isolation); a pod reports through GitHub statuses that N-04 reads.
many-agents.collision: Two callers Commit one operation key: the writer serializes them; the first commits 201; the second with the same request hash gets the stored reply 200 replayed; with a different hash it gets 409 idempotency_mismatch and nothing is written.
One run has six effects (bundle, workspace, result, push, PR, review): each has its own key from shared/contracts.xml#operation-keys, so none can be answered with another's reply.
Two callers write one entity at one expected version: one commits; the other gets 409 reason version with the current version and re-reads.
A run whose lease expired or was revoked writes again: its token is not current and the Commit is 412, except the one terminal report shared/contracts.xml#terminal-report admits.
A process in group coq-store sends records naming another node or by: step 0 derives node and by from its uid and answers 403 principal_mismatch; nothing is written.
Two writers mint one record id: the UNIQUE index refuses the second with 409 reason id; the writer re-mints and retries, up to 3 times.
N-05 snapshots while nodes commit: the copy is one read transaction on its own connection; commits continue; the copy names its own high-water seq.
many-agents.test: Two processes and four goroutines Commit 1000 requests each with overlapping operation keys, entities and lease tokens: exactly one row set per key, every 409 and 412 logged, seq strictly increasing and unique (gaps allowed), no seq reused after a delete, hash recomputed equals stored.

emits.note: replayed=true: the operation key and request hash were already committed

emits.acts: the caller and N-31, which fans the cursor out
the caller fixes its request; 3 in a minute from one node is reported by N-06 health
nobody automatically; N-51 counts them and any from an unknown uid is an owner alert
nobody for the old holder; N-12 and N-11 already acted; the record is evidence
owner: the line stays held until an owner ruling releases it (shared/contracts.xml#restore); every Tail client resnapshots
owner, alerted by the outside probe; the prepared restore plan is in the runbook
N-06 health; the runbook checkpoint step
N-45 cleanup runs first; then the owner through a card
owner, alerted by the outside probe (shared/outside-probe.xml#alerting); written to the outage journal and imported on recovery
the Tail client reconnects from its cursor

status-codes.rule: Every code above must exist in ../../shared/status-codes.xml#codes with the same meaning and actor. cursor.expired (410) is a Tail and List reply, not a record.

path.cleanup: systemd removes /run/coq at stop; scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-run.sh removes a stale socket when no pid holds it

path.writer: N-01: a pre-allocated file of store.reserve_mib, deleted once under the free-space floor and re-created above floor plus reserve (shared/outside-probe.xml#journal)
path.cleanup: never a cleanup target; listed so scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-run.sh skips it by name
scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-run.sh removes it after store.restored or a SERVING open

path.writer: N-01 structured log, one line per Commit over 100 ms and per non-2xx

state-paths.rule: STATE is the coq-svc state root; nothing under it is ever committed. Every cleanup script defaults to dry-run; --apply deletes; both exit 0 on nothing to do, 3 when the unit is running and the path is live.
cleanup-store.sh refuses --apply unless the unit is stopped and N-05 lists a verified backup whose epoch is the current epoch and whose high_water_seq is the store's.

edges.in: every output of every node is a Commit; the return writes are not drawn

out.record: Snapshot reply on a reader connection

item.check: coq.db opens in WAL mode with synchronous FULL and busy_timeout 5000.
item.proof: PRAGMA values printed by `scheduler ctl store pragmas` in the test log (not-run).

item.proof: Go test with three socket peers under distinct uids (not-run).

A Commit carrying entities, statements, records and effects commits all or none; any failing step leaves the file unchanged.
item.proof: Go test injecting a failure at each step (not-run).

item.proof: Go test with a lease swept and re-granted (not-run).

Snapshot does not hold the writer: commits continue during VACUUM INTO and the reply's numbers match the copy.
item.proof: Go test with a writer loop measuring latency during Snapshot (not-run; baseline probe numbers in #mechanism).

item.check: Tail with a cursor of an older epoch or below min_retained_seq is OUT_OF_RANGE cursor.expired.
A restore drill starts epoch n+1 held with flags off, every lease expired and counter:lease_token past every token issued before, and appends store.restored.
item.proof: Integration test: restore an older backup over a store with live leases (not-run).

No path under the repository is written.
item.proof: `git status --porcelain` empty after the full test run (not-run).

item.check: Every state path above has its cleanup script, dry-run by default; every emitted code is in the shared map.

permissions.rule: Authority is the caller's Unix identity mapped by shared/authority.xml#principals and #role-derivation; no field a caller sends grants anything; COQ_SEAT is diagnostic only.

actor.name: service (coq-svc, nodes in-process)
actor.may: Commit through Store.Do as the node the op names, only that node's kinds and registered statements; Get, List, Tail, Snapshot

actor.name: launcher (coq-launch, socket)
actor.may: Commit only the kinds and statements shared/authority.xml#role-derivation grants the launcher (seat.result, the seat heartbeat entity, the run entity, lease Start, Renew and Release through N-02's statements), each under the run's lease; Get of its own runs

actor.name: pod
actor.may: nothing here; reports through GitHub statuses

actor.name: owner (socket, ctl CLI)
actor.may: Get, List, Tail; Commit of owner-surface kinds; a direct sqlite3 session on the live file is break glass, with the unit stopped, recorded before and after

permissions.rule: The socket is 0660 coq-svc:coq-store under /run/coq; there is no TCP listener.

counter.name: store.commit_latency_ms
counter.alarm: p99 over 500 ms for 3 health ticks

check.name: store.health
check.ok: SELECT 1 under 100 ms and free space above the floor
check.else: 503 store.unavailable or store.disk, latched: one record per transition, journaled when the store cannot take it

monitoring.surface: Counters appear in the Status answer (N-06), on Stats (N-40) and the Machine panel (N-39); store-down reaches the owner through the outside probe, not through the store.

runbook.task: `scheduler ctl store status` prints epoch, high-water seq, min retained seq, db and wal bytes, tail clients, last checkpoint. Read-only.
`scheduler ctl record get ID` or `scheduler ctl record list --after EPOCH:SEQ --kind KIND`.
`scheduler ctl store checkpoint` (PASSIVE); only when store.wal_large fired; it changes no data.

Follow shared/contracts.xml#restore step by step; this node's part: (1) stop coq-svc.service and coq-launch.service; (2) `scheduler/host/bin/restore-store.sh --from BACKUP --dry-run` prints the backup's epoch and high_water_seq and the live file's high-water seq, so the lost range is known before anything moves; (3) `--apply` moves the live file aside with a UTC stamp, copies the backup, runs integrity_check and starts the service in restore mode, where the socket admits only the owner; (4) the first Commit (N-01/store.restored/<epoch>/r1) starts the next epoch, sets the hold, turns build mode off, raises counter:lease_token by the margin of #restore and expires every reserved or running lease; (5) after reconciliation by N-04, N-09, N-23 and the outbox, store.restored 200 names the epoch, the backup and what was found; (6) only an owner ruling releases the hold.
scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-store.sh, cleanup-run.sh, cleanup-logs.sh as listed in state-paths; dry-run first, always.
A direct `sqlite3 STATE/store/coq.db` write session is owner-only, one time, as coq-svc with the units stopped, recorded as break.glass before and after.

item.what: NATS JetStream as the store or wake bus
item.reason: C34 ruled no broker; the failure class was addressing, which a broker stores but does not fix (S03 F3)

item.what: one file per record and one file per job in the state root as the store
item.reason: a directory of files has no compare-and-swap, no sequence and no single-writer guarantee; the record id form and the append-only principle are kept (V01)

item.what: the executor runs events/bin/event.sh to write records
item.reason: the store is the writer; event.sh's validation moves into Commit; event.sh becomes the ctl CLI's `record add` verb

item.what: no streaming call on the control plane (h-proto-stream)
item.reason: D21 (C52) rules push; Tail is the one server stream, limited to cursor fan-out; the no-stream rule stays for every other RPC

item.what: the repository copy of the record log and the three stranded roots
item.reason: two sources of truth (K07); N-49 reconciles them into this store once, then deletes

item.what: PostgreSQL or Redis behind the service
item.reason: a second daemon on a host with eleven bugchecks; SQLite needs none and survives a process kill

item.what: Put with one record and one entity, keyed by a caller-chosen idempotency key compared by key only (book 1.0)
item.reason: no node could write its own tables atomically and six effects shared one key; Commit with operation keys and request hashes replaces it (F02, F04)

item.what: a same-user 0600 socket and caller-supplied node and by (book 1.0)
item.reason: any process of the owner, a seat included, could write any kind as any node; SO_PEERCRED and server-derived identity replace it (F01)

item.what: Snapshot by VACUUM INTO under the writer's turn (book 1.0)
item.reason: it blocks every commit for the copy's duration (report D: 2.82 s on 293.7 MiB); a reader connection copies the same image without holding the writer
